rich_summary: After the burning of the lac house, the citizens of Varanavata believe the Pandavas have perished in the fire set by Purochana at Duryodhana’s command, and they bitterly condemn Dhritarashtra and the conspirators. In truth, the Pandavas escape through the secret tunnel prepared earlier. Exhausted and moving through darkness with their mother Kunti, they are carried by the powerful Bhima, who bears all his family as he forces a path through the forest. Meanwhile, Vidura—aware of the plot through spies—secretly sends a trusted agent who finds them near the Ganga and provides a specially prepared boat. Using coded words from Vidura as proof of loyalty, the agent ferries them across the river and urges secrecy. Back in the city, the townspeople discover the burned lac house and the bodies of a Nishada woman and her sons, mistakenly believing the Pandavas are dead, while the hidden escape tunnel is carefully concealed.

highlight_spans.why: The shocked citizens lament the supposed death of the Pandavas and condemn Dhritarashtra and Purochana, revealing the moral outrage surrounding the plot.
The crucial revelation that the Pandavas escaped through the subterranean passage while the town believed them dead.
Bhima’s extraordinary act of carrying his mother and brothers through the forest emphasizes his strength and the family’s unity in crisis.
Vidura’s secret intervention—sending a trusted agent and a specially prepared boat—shows his loyalty and political foresight.
The townspeople’s discovery of the burned bodies and the concealed tunnel underscores the success of the Pandavas’ deception.

top_scenes.scene_text: Bhima strides through the dark forest carrying Kunti on his shoulder and his brothers on his arms and sides while trees bend and break before his immense strength.
On the misty banks of the Ganga at night, Vidura’s secret agent reveals a swift, bannered boat to the weary Pandavas as they prepare for their hidden escape.
The townspeople stand before the smoldering ruins of the lac house at dawn, lamenting what they believe are the burned bodies of the Pandavas.
